title: Automated Compliance Audit Orchestration
business: Financial institutions requiring strict adherence to regulatory reporting standards.
problem: Generalist agents often hallucinate complex compliance logic or fail to maintain the required audit trail when handling multi-step document verification.
solution: Implement a manager agent that maintains control of the user session, utilizing specialized compliance agents as bounded tools via Agent.as_tool() to perform isolated verification tasks without losing the overall audit context.
steps: Define a Manager Agent with high-level oversight instructions and session state management.
Create specialized agents for specific tasks like 'Tax Code Validator' and 'Identity Verifier'.
Expose these specialized agents to the Manager Agent using the Agent.as_tool() method.
Configure the Manager Agent to invoke these tools sequentially or conditionally based on document type.
Aggregate tool outputs into a final, human-readable compliance report within the Manager Agent.
outcome: Improved accuracy in regulatory reporting and a centralized, traceable audit log managed by a single point of authority.
limitation: The manager agent may become a bottleneck if it attempts to process too many concurrent tool calls; monitor latency by checking the time elapsed between tool invocation and result aggregation.

diagram.title: Compliance Delegation Loop
diagram.description: The Manager Agent orchestrates the flow by calling specialists as tools.

code.content:
# Define the specialist agent
tax_agent = Agent(name="TaxValidator")
# Expose as a tool to the manager
manager.add_tool(tax_agent.as_tool())
# Manager retains control of the conversation flow
response = manager.run(user_input)
code.explanation: This maps to the scenario by allowing the Manager Agent to treat the TaxValidator as a bounded tool, ensuring the manager retains control of the final output.

questions.question: In Automated Compliance Audit Orchestration, why is the manager-as-tool pattern preferred over generalist agents?
options: It prevents hallucination by keeping the manager in control of the audit context.
It allows specialists to take over the user-facing conversation entirely.
It eliminates the need for any specialized agents in the workflow.
It automatically reduces the cost of every API call by 50 percent.
questions.explanation: The problem states generalist agents hallucinate; the solution uses the manager to maintain context and control, ensuring specialists act only as bounded tools.
questions.evidence: Generalist agents often hallucinate complex compliance logic or fail to maintain the required audit trail when handling multi-step document verification.

questions.question: What is a primary limitation of the implementation in Automated Compliance Audit Orchestration?
options: The manager agent cannot call more than one tool at a time.
The manager agent may become a bottleneck if it processes too many concurrent tool calls.
Specialist agents cannot return data back to the manager.
The system requires a manual human-in-the-loop for every single tool call.
questions.explanation: The limitation section explicitly identifies the manager becoming a bottleneck as a risk when scaling tool calls.
questions.evidence: The manager agent may become a bottleneck if it attempts to process too many concurrent tool calls; monitor latency by checking the time elapsed between tool invocation and result aggregation.
